column1: # The Phase-2 relocation map — one row per moved prefix, authored before the move.
# exist *before* any relocation runs, so `tools/repository_conformance_gate.py` compares
# the tree against a plan rather than against itself. A gate that read the tree and then
# declared it conforming would pass on any tree at all.
#   old_prefix   the present-day path, exactly as the tree carried it before the move.
#                A trailing slash means a directory prefix; no trailing slash means one
#                file. Rows are applied longest-prefix-first, so a nested row
#   new_prefix   the destination. The gate refuses a destination
#                `repository_layout_doctrine.md` section 2 does not admit, which is what
#                mutant m3 seeds: a map that lies is caught before the tree is touched.
#   license      why the move is licensed. Either the verbatim first-column cell of a
#                destination needed deciding — or `seven-noun-rule` for a `test/`
#                second level that is simply an eighth role, which section 2 calls
#                non-conforming on sight. A row citing neither is a defect.
# The map covers relocation only. A *deletion* stays with its last consumer, which is
# why no row here names `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN/evidence/**` or `test/enumeration/**`: a root
# cannot be deleted while a phase still builds from it, but a rename plus its reference
# update is one edit with no last consumer to wait for.
# --- Sprint 2.1: test/'s second level collapses to the seven role nouns --------------
# The singular/plural pairs come first because a case-insensitive filesystem cannot hold
# `test/ui/` and `test/Ui/` apart at all: on APFS they are one directory that git's index
# remembers as two, so a bulk move of one silently carries the other.
# Module hierarchy belongs below test/spec/, never at test/'s second level.
# Positive inputs, rejected inputs, and boundary shims, each to its role noun.
# --- Sprint 2.3: the package-only roots become cabal stanzas ------------------------
# Section 2.1's criterion is *separately resolvable, never merely separately configured*.
# None of these roots meets it: each is one `hs-source-dirs` and a component list, which
# cabal answers inside the one authored package. The sources move to the root their
# reader owns — GHC's `src/`, protoc's `proto/`, the Dhall interpreter's `dhall/`, and
# the seven test role nouns — and the `.cabal` file itself is not relocated at all: it
# becomes a stanza, so Sprint 2.3 removes it rather than moving it.
